subject: EHR integration: PHI handling, privacy assessment and BAA exceptions
messages:
From: Eva Clark <eva.clark@riverhealth.org>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@riverhealth.org
Date: Sat, 24 May 2025 20:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Detailed PHI handling & BAA terms for EHR integration

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding chat earlier this week. We're working through vendor risk and legal review for the planned EHR integration and need a compact, answerable package to present to our security and legal teams by end of day Friday (May 30). Can you provide the following items: 

1) Clear statement whether Redwood will receive or persist PHI when integrated via FHIR ingestion or HL7 feeds.
2) Diagram of data flow from RiverHealth EHR -> Redwood -> customer app, including any ephemeral caches and logs.
3) Encryption details: algorithms for data at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM usage, and key rotation cadence.
4) Retention & deletion controls: how can we request deletion and what timelines?
5) Subprocessor list and any planned cloud vendor regions where PHI may transit or be stored.
6) SOC 2 and relevant attestations; pending reports and expected dates.
7) A copy of your standard BAA and whether you can accept a small set of exceptions around limited data residency constraints.
8) Any technical mitigations you recommend for minimizing PHI surface during EHR sync (tokenization, redaction, pre-ingest suppression).

If you can attach a draft BAA and a short one-page summary for our security reviewers that would be ideal. We may request a redline — please note our procurement deadline.

Best,
Eva
Eva Clark
Manager, Vendor Risk
RiverHealth Systems

Attachments: RiverHealth_Vendor_Risk_Template.xlsx (we will attach when we send official RFP)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Clark <eva.clark@riverhealth.org>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 May 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed PHI handling & BAA terms for EHR integration

Hi Eva — thanks, and appreciated the clear list. I'm attaching a short summary and a draft BAA to start (see attachments). Below are quick answers to your numbered items; Rishi from engineering and Marissa from Product are cc'ed and will follow up with any technical artifacts.

1) PHI persistence: Redwood does not persist PHI in hosted mode beyond application-configured retention windows unless the customer explicitly stores persistent records. For FHIR/HL7 ingestion we support transient processing and can be configured to avoid persisting identifiers; however, customers often choose to persist normalized records in their tenant. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers control data residency and persistence.

2) Data flow: attached is a one-page summary. High level: EHR -> TLS -> Redwood ingestion endpoint -> optional transformation layer (tokenization/redaction) -> temporary KV cache for inference -> optional long-term store controlled by customer. Logs are redacted by default to remove PHI fields.

3) Encryption: TLS 1.2/1.3 for in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest. We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with BYOK/HSM options for Dedicated/Private. Key rotation policies are configurable; default rotation 90 days.

4) Retention/deletion: Customers can set retention per-route. Deletion requests are honored via a single-API purge endpoint with confirmation; standard SLA for purge is 7 business days for hosted, same-day for Dedicated when coordinated. We also support retention holds for legal exceptions.

5) Subprocessors & regions: we maintain a publicly available subprocessor list; for PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private in your preferred US region to avoid cross-region transit. Subprocessor list attached as part of our compliance pack.

6) Attestations: SOC 2 Type II is available on request; annual penetration test summaries are provided under NDA. Current SOC 2 cycle completes Q3 2025; we can provide the report as soon as it's released.

7) BAA: attached is our standard BAA for review. We can accept narrowly scoped data residency exceptions for Dedicated/Private setups; please share the specific language you need and we'll route to Legal.

8) Mitigations: recommend pre-ingest tokenization, schema-based redaction, and customer-side pseudonymization. We can run an onboarding pilot to demonstrate the flow with synthetic data.

Next steps: I've attached 'Redwood_PHI_Data_Summary_20250525.pdf' and 'BAA_DRAFT_RiverHealth_v1_20250525.docx'. Can we set a 30-minute technical call mid-week to walk your security and engineering teams through the network diagram?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_PHI_Data_Summary_20250525.pdf; BAA_DRAFT_RiverHealth_v1_20250525.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Eva Clark <eva.clark@riverhealth.org>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 May 2025 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed PHI handling & BAA terms for EHR integration

Eva / team — looping in some technical detail so you have concrete answers for security. Attaching a network diagram and crypto PRD. High-level notes below; happy to expand on any item on the call.

- Ingestion: we accept FHIR JSON over HTTPS or HL7 v2 over MLLP (TLS). We recommend TLS 1.3 endpoints with mutual TLS for higher-assurance integrations.
- Transient vs persistent: our ingestion pipeline writes to an isolated processing tier. For hosted customers we persist derived artifacts only when the customer requests storage; raw PHI is not indexed in search by default and is scrubbed from logs.
- Caching: KV cache holds model state only; we do not persist raw PHI tokens in the cache beyond configured TTL. Cache eviction and encrypted memory are enforced.
- Encryption & keys: AES-256-GCM at rest; TLS 1.3 in transit. For Dedicated/Private, we support HSM-backed keys with customer-controlled KMS. Key access is logged; rotation automation available via API.
- Data deletion: purge API is idempotent and returns deletion receipts. For hosted customers purge SLA is 7 business days; for Dedicated we can arrange same-day emulated purge when coordinated with infra.
- Auditing & logs: request-level logging is pseudonymized; full request bodies containing PHI are stored encrypted with separate KMS and accessible only under strict RBAC.
- Subprocessors: core inference runs on our managed clusters (we name primary compute provider in the subprocessor list); we do not re-sell or share PHI with analytics partners.
- EHR-specific mitigations: we can support a pre-ingest proxy at your side to tokenise sensitive identifiers before sending, and we offer FHIR schema filters to drop fields.

Attachments: network-diagram-phi.png; crypto-PRD-2025.pdf

If RiverHealth requires a data residency clause that prevents any PHI from leaving a given US region, recommended path is Redwood Dedicated with region pinning.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
